guide.title: Cardiac Anatomy & Physiology
guide.lead: You don't need a textbook heart in the field, just enough to predict trouble. Which artery feeds which wall tells you what an MI will do. Which pacemaker is firing tells you how slow the heart can go. And cardiac output = rate × volume tells you why both too fast and too slow can cause shock.

sections.title: Four chambers, four valves
notes: S1 ("lub") = mitral and tricuspid closing. S2 ("dub") = aortic and pulmonic closing.
The coronary arteries fill mainly in diastole, so a very fast rate can starve the heart muscle.

Lateral ST elevation; can be electrically quiet
Right ventricle, inferior wall, and in most people the SA and AV nodes

sections.title: Pacemakers: who takes over
notes: The AV node delay lets the atria empty first (atrial kick).
The slower and wider the escape, the lower it sits and the less reliable it is.

groups.title: Rate problems
items: Too slow: not enough beats (heart block)
Too fast: no time to fill (rapid VT, SVT)

groups.title: Volume problems
items: Preload low: bleeding, dehydration, nitrates in RV infarction

quiz.q: Which valve separates the left atrium from the left ventricle?
quiz.explanation: Tricuspid on the right, mitral on the left.

quiz.q: Which part of the conduction system is the natural pacemaker, firing at 60–100/min?
quiz.explanation: If it fails, the AV junction (40–60/min) or the ventricles (20–40/min) take over.

options: The mitral and tricuspid valves closing
The aortic and pulmonic valves closing
Blood flowing in the coronary arteries
quiz.explanation: S2 is the semilunar valves closing.

quiz.q: Which chamber has the thickest wall?
ST elevation in the anterior leads points to a blocked:
quiz.explanation: The LAD feeds the anterior wall and septum.

quiz.q: Why does an inferior MI often cause bradycardia or heart block?
options: The right coronary artery usually supplies the SA and AV nodes
The LAD supplies the AV node
Pain triggers the vagus nerve in every MI
quiz.explanation: Watch the rate and prepare to pace.

quiz.q: A ventricular escape rhythm usually runs at:

quiz.explanation: BP = cardiac output × systemic vascular resistance.

quiz.q: Why can a very fast heart rate cause chest pain even with normal arteries?
options: The coronaries fill in diastole, which gets too short
Fast rates raise the oxygen in the blood
The SA node runs out of energy
quiz.explanation: Less filling time for both the ventricles and the coronaries.

options: Increases rate, contractility and conduction speed
quiz.explanation: The vagus nerve does the opposite to the rate.

flashcards.question: Four chambers; thickest wall?
flashcards.answer: Right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, left ventricle. The left ventricle is thickest: it pumps against systemic resistance.

flashcards.question: AV valves vs semilunar valves
flashcards.answer: AV: tricuspid (right) and mitral (left). Semilunar: pulmonic (right) and aortic (left).

flashcards.question: Three main coronary arteries
flashcards.answer: LAD: anterior wall and septum. Circumflex: lateral wall. Right coronary: right ventricle, inferior wall, and in most people the SA and AV nodes.

flashcards.question: Blood flow through the heart
flashcards.answer: Venae cavae → right atrium → tricuspid → right ventricle → pulmonic → lungs → pulmonary veins → left atrium → mitral → left ventricle → aortic valve → aorta.

flashcards.question: Systole vs diastole
flashcards.answer: Systole: ventricles contract and eject. Diastole: ventricles relax and fill, and the coronary arteries fill.

flashcards.question: Conduction system, in order
flashcards.answer: SA node (60–100/min) → AV node → bundle of His → bundle branches → Purkinje fibres. Escapes: junction 40–60/min, ventricles 20–40/min.

flashcards.question: Why the AV node delay matters
flashcards.answer: It lets the atria empty into the ventricles before they contract (atrial kick).

flashcards.question: Sympathetic effect on the heart
flashcards.answer: Via beta-1: faster rate, stronger contraction, quicker conduction.

flashcards.question: Cardiac output
flashcards.answer: Heart rate × stroke volume. Stroke volume depends on preload, contractility and afterload.

critical.scenario: A 58-year-old has crushing chest pain for 45 minutes. BP 104/68, HR 118, SpO₂ 96%. The 12-lead shows ST elevation in V1–V4. He becomes short of breath and you hear crackles at both bases.
critical.question: Which artery is blocked, and why the crackles?

options.t: LAD: the anterior wall is failing, so blood backs up into the lungs
options.f: Correct. A large anterior MI causes acute pump failure.
V1–V4 is the anterior wall; RV failure gives clear lungs and raised JVP.
Lateral MI shows in I, aVL, V5–V6.
New crackles during an anterior MI are pump failure until proven otherwise.

critical.explanation: Expect cardiogenic shock: pre-notify the PCI centre, sit him up and avoid large fluid boluses.
critical.kpi: Correlates ECG territory with coronary anatomy and recognizes acute pump failure

critical.scenario: A 72-year-old fainted for 15 seconds. BP 102/64, HR 38, lightheaded. The monitor shows regular P waves that don't relate to the wide QRS complexes at 38/min.
critical.question: What's happening in the conduction system?

options.t: Complete heart block: nothing gets through the AV node, and a slow ventricular escape drives the heart
options.f: Correct. The wide QRS shows the escape sits low.
In first-degree block every P wave is followed by a QRS.
There are clear, regular P waves.
Syncope with a rate of 38 is not normal.

critical.explanation: Ventricular escapes (20–40/min) are slow and unreliable: prepare to pace and transport.
critical.kpi: Recognizes complete heart block and its impact on cardiac output from conduction system dysfunction

critical.scenario: A 45-year-old with poorly controlled hypertension has sudden tearing chest pain through to his back. BP 188/104 right arm, 146/88 left arm. The left radial pulse is weaker. No STEMI on the 12-lead.
critical.question: What does the arm difference suggest?

options.t: Aortic dissection involving the arch branches
options.f: Correct. A difference above 20 mmHg or a pulse deficit supports it.
That doesn't cause a pressure difference between arms.

options.t: A faulty BP cuff, so ignore it
options.f: Recheck, but a real difference is a red flag.
PE doesn't cause unequal arm pressures.

critical.explanation: Withhold aspirin if dissection is suspected and transport fast to a centre with cardiothoracic surgery.
critical.kpi: Recognizes aortic dissection anatomy and the significance of BP differential/pulse deficits
